patch_description:
This approach abandons the greedy/local-search paradigm entirely and instead exploits a fundamental additive-combinatorics identity: for a Sidon set (all pairwise sums distinct), |A+A| = n(n+1)/2 and |A-A| = n(n-1)+1, giving ratio ~2. This is the theoretical maximum for the sum/difference ratio. So the optimal strategy is to build the *largest* Sidon set possible within a bounded integer range, then apply small "sum-compacting" perturbations that preserve the Sidon property locally but reduce |A+A| slightly (e.g., by introducing a few coincidental sums while keeping all differences distinct).

The key insight: Bose-Chowla / Singer constructions give Sidon sets of size p in range ~p². We use the Ruzsa construction A = {2pk + (k² mod p) : k=0..p-1} which is a perfect difference set (|A-A| = p(p-1)+1) with |A+A| ≤ p(p+1)/2 + extra. We sweep p up to ~1000 (yielding sets of size ~1000 with |A-A| ~ 10^6 and |A+A| ~ 5×10^5), then apply a final "sum compaction" pass that tries to shrink |A+A| without losing differences by replacing one element with a nearby value that shares many sums.

This is fundamentally different: instead of stochastic search it uses a deterministic algebraic construction with provably near-optimal sum/difference ratio, scaled to maximize the log-ratio (which grows with size due to the (1-1/|A|)/100 bonus).
